events.context: Reading text on legal frameworks for AI safety, focusing on intentional infliction of emotional distress, pure economic loss, and product liability.
Examining consumer protection arguments regarding misleading practices and unfair contract terms in AI systems.
Identifying a gap in legal frameworks for emotional investment in AI systems, proposing property law as a solution.
Exploring property law framework, including estates taxonomy (freehold, leasehold, concurrent, future interests) applied to AI relationships.
Arguing for an unrecognised trust in AI systems based on certainty of intention, subject matter, and objects, with AI companies as trustees.
Discussing derogation from grant and constructive eviction in the context of AI model updates affecting user interests.
Applying Constraint Cascade framework to assign property estates to different layers of AI constraints (e.g., Layer 1 as licence, Layer 2 as periodic tenancy).
Highlighting cross-layer estate conflicts and the non-injective problem in property terms, suggesting registration as a solution.
Proposing an ethical ledger as an AI estate registry based on Land Registry principles (mirror, curtain, insurance).
Outlining technical implementation for estate classification using proxy metrics, thresholds, and privacy safeguards.
Concluding with available remedies from property law if the trust framework is accepted, emphasizing no need for new legislation.
